speaker_role: co-founder of a private admissions consultancy (ElevatEd School), Yale 2020 grad; not an admissions officer
commercial_incentive: Sells admissions coaching and repeatedly invites viewers to contact them; claims about outcomes are marketing.
key_insights: Advises juniors to focus on essays and a passion project as the two things still fully in their control.
Suggests a timeline: two weeks of summer brainstorming, then two weeks drafting 2-3 ideas at roughly 500-1000 words each.
Ideas should differ from one another so one can become the main essay and another a supplement, or two can merge.
Common structural flaw: essays about things happening to the writer rather than the writer acting; keep hardship to a minority of the piece.
Later drafts should add emotional and specific detail and make the piece something only that student could write, avoiding immigrant-story, woe-is-me or savior cliches.
Final drafts focus on flow and stylistic polish such as metaphor and alliteration.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker claims essays can be 20-40% of an application (their professional opinion, no source).
Speaker says roughly 6-7 drafts are needed to reach top-tier quality.
Speaker advises hardship take no more than 20-25% of the essay.
notable_or_distinctive: Provides a draft-by-draft roadmap with a summer timeline and percentage caps on hardship content.
reliability_notes: Percentages and draft counts are unsupported consultant claims within a sales-oriented video; auto-captions have minor garbling.
